notes.title: Five Days After The Watcher Launch
notes.content:
Hey slugcats,

I’m Joseph, but some of you know me as riv otter, and I’m the community manager for Akupara Games. Rain World was actually where I got my start for community management with Rain World Art Month and Anniversary events!

Hope you have been enjoying playing [i]Rain World: The Watcher[/i]. Exploring the new mechanics that the Watcher brings with them to traverse through the hazardous regions. 

I do want to take the opportunity to speak about some of the plans for the future of [i]The Watcher[/i]. 

[h2]Bugfixes[/h2]
If you’ve ever wondered who goes through all the feedback and bug reports after a big release like this one– well, the answer is me!. I do want to thank you for your patience on this as we are a small indie team and going through all the reports and investigating each of them is going to take us a bit  of time. Our plans is to keep patching as rapidly as possible to solve issues and add more qualities of life options for players. At a certain point in a few weeks, we’ll be a little quieter as things get in gear for our console updates.

[h2]Post-release Content[/h2]
Even as we speak, the developer team is energized with ideas and we’re organizing them for release both in the short and long-term.. Our short term priorities include additions like those bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements I mentioned above while long term priorities include additions like James mentioned a few weeks ago– the final endings and other cryptic secrets. We’re looking to start dropping patches with some of that content in about a week and we can’t for you to experience them. 

I would like to talk about them a bit but the developer team, specifically James, would send the wrath of 1,000s of [spoiler]blizzard lizards[/spoiler] and [spoiler]barnacles[/spoiler] to my house if I made even the tiniest peep. May even send rain as well to add insult to injury…

[h2]Consoles[/h2]
I’ve seen a lot of questions about consoles, so here is an update: The DLC is definitely coming out this year on consoles with plans to release within six months. There’s always trouble porting [i]Rain World[/i] onto the Nintendo Switch because of the nature of the hardware constraints but we’ve done it before and we’ll do it again. If Switch delays the console ports too much, we may end up pushing just Switch to a later date.

Either way, we’re looking to release a lot more Watcher content this spring and summer! 

I’ll have more to share once the next patch comes out, but until then– thank you all so much for another amazing launch!

- Riv Otter

notes.title: Rain World: The Watcher Out Now!
notes.content:
Hey Slugcats,

[h2][i]Rain World: The Watcher[/i] is Out Now![/h2]
[previewyoutube=_pb8eP0jetI;full][/previewyoutube]

Journey beyond to something, somewhere only ever glimpsed. When the world beneath your feet cracks and crumbles, will you hold on to all you once knew? Or dive into the unknown?

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2857120/Rain_World_The_Watcher/ 

[h3]Mods before The Watcher[/h3]
Most community mods from the workshop will be incompatible with The Watcher DLC at launch. I would strongly recommend you unsubscribe from the community mods and do a full reinstall of Rain World by deleting, moving, or renaming the Rain World folder typically located at C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Rain World. Then verify the files through Steam.

You may also need to remove your Rain World saves. Your saves should be located in C:\Users\[[YOUR_USER]]\AppData\LocalLow\Videocult\Rain World. Change [[YOUR_USER]] to your username on your PC.

The files will be named "sav", "sav2", or "sav3" depending on which save slot it is used.
 
[h3]Additional Workshop Tags[/h3]
To help out with filtering through the mods and to give modders access to better communicate with their mods, I have added a “Compatible With” section where you can add which part of Rain World and DLCs your mod works with. The tags are “Base”, “Downpour”, and “Watcher”.

[h3]Where to Report Bugs?[/h3]
We are trying something different for bug reporting so please be patient with us! If you run into any bugs while playing The Watcher, then please report them here so we can better track the reports.
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSezXL3WE2udFn8qJn-4bKHf-YkxiIbzmLB6jSwP6XYfp8DJtQ/viewform?usp=header

- Riv otter

[*] Fixed one of Saint's tutorial messages not appearing as it should.
[*] Fixed dream illustrations being off-centered in lower resolutions and some buttons being cut off at lower resolutions.
[*] Fixed hidden challenges in Expedition mode not being counted towards the Total Challenges Completed counter.
[*] Various small tweaks to some of the regions (a few extra shelters, some spawn changes, etc.)

notes.content:

I hope you have been keeping Gourmand well fed and Artificer away from the scavs. Over the weekend we released another patch to fix various bugs including echoes in Expedition mode putting the player's karma cap into a broken state and adding an extra 16:10 aspect ratio resolution option for better display on Steam Deck. [*] When only one player is left in Co-op mode, fix the Game Over screen not appearing when a lizard grabs you but doesn't kill you.
[*] Dialog text now properly reverts back to white colored text when the text should no longer be colored.

notes.title: Rain World: Downpour is out now!
notes.content:
Hey, slugcats!

It is time for me to finally pass Gourmand to you guys. You better take good care of them and keep them well fed. [i]Rain World: Downpour[/i] is out now!
 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bDDUnWnjdK0

[h3]Rain World: Downpour features[/h3]
[list]
[*] 5 new playable slugcat campaigns
[*] New regions and rooms
[*] Co Op campaign mode
[*] Expedition mode
[*] Challenge mode
[*] Safari mode
[/list]
Even if you don’t get [i]Downpour[/i], [i]Rain World[/i] is receiving a free update for the first time in many years that includes new resources for players and modders of Rain World.

[h3]Rain World: Remix features[/h3]
[list]
[*] Steam Workshop
[*] In game mod loader
[*] Russian and Chinese languages
[*] Accessibility options
[*] Bug fixes
[/list]
[b]Note:[/b] If you have modded your files, then [i]Rain World: Remix[/i] will not launch. You will need to do a complete reinstall of [i]Rain World[/i]. Remove the [i]Rain World[/i] folder from Steam. The folder will typically be located in C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Rain World then verify the game files.

Uninstalling the game through Steam does not delete all files and so you must manually delete the Rain World folder and then reinstall through Steam.

One more final note with the launch of Downpour and Remix. We have set up two branches on Steam so if you like to revert back to ver. 1.5 or ver. 1.01 for any reason then you can. Right click Rain World in the library and click properties. Under the “beta” tab, you can select the 1.5 build by selecting “legacy” or select 1.01 build by selecting “legacy” from the drop down menu.

Rain World: Downpour adds so much content to a game beloved by the community. We’ve been very honored to work with such an amazing community to develop Downpour. Again be sure to give thanks to all the amazing community members who worked on developing the DLC. You can view who from the community worked on Downpour here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/312520/view/5507370455348858235?l=english

notes.title: Expedition Mode Dev Log
notes.content:
Hey, slugcats!

Yesterday, w- wait, Gourmand check first. Gourmand pushed over the whole fridge just to get the cookie jar on top of the fridge. I still have to come up with a way to explain this to the boss…

Yesterday, we revealed that Expedition Mode will be coming to Rain World: Downpour! If you missed the trailer, you can watch it here!
https://youtu.be/H7tVAwwmHaE
Expedition mode brings a new and exciting way to play Rain World! Each campaign you can set up different challenges, difficulty, slugcats and more! Complete the challenges to gain points to unlock perks, burdens, music for the jukebox and more!

[h2]Meet the Developer[/h2]
Expedition Mode was developed by the amazing, talented LeeMoriya! He also developed some exceptional Rain World mods like Forecast and In-Game Warp Menu. And for other mod developers out there, he has been super helpful in the modding scene by helping players that are having trouble with modding their game. Here is a message from LeeMoriya himself!

“Hey Everyone,

I hope you've enjoyed what you've seen of Expedition so far, I'm excited to see your reactions once you get your hands on it. While the new mode is tailored more towards hardcore players and completionists, I hope everyone can find something about Expedition they enjoy.

Rain World's modding community is the first one I've ever become really invested in, and without their help and support, Expedition and many of my other mods may never have been made. So If I've ever bugged you for help, or you've enjoyed something I've made, then I'd like to thank you!

-LeeMoriya”

[h2]Selecting a Slugcat[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8051219/76e256f286b76716ab20797d125b20f61a4ab7da.jpg[/img]
Your first decision in Expedition Mode will always be what slugcat you’d like to play. If you have More Slugcats expansion enabled, then you’ll be able to use them as well! You must have beaten the slugcat's campaign before you can select them in Expedition Mode! Selecting a slugcat will have their special spawns and abilities! So Rivulet still rockets across the map and the Artificer explodes with their jumps.

You can have one expedition save for each slugcat per save file.

[h2]Selecting Challenges[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8051219/66176f013f70a199e31ae8025495cba518ad9991.jpg[/img]
Once you have your slugcat selected, you then be able to select your challenges! You may have up to 5 challenges active in an expedition. The more challenges you face and complete the more points you will earn at the end of the run which will help you unlock stuff. 

Here are the different types of challenges you can face:
[list]
[*] Passage
[*] Echo
[*] Score
[*] Hunting
[*] Item collecting
[*] Pearl delivery / hoarding
[*] Neuron gifting 
[*] Spear pinning
[*] Vista visiting
[/list]
You may filter these so you only get the challenges you like! 

The difficulty of the challenges can be selected with the slider bar over the challenges. The more difficult the challenges are, the more points you may earn at the end of the expedition. You may make the expedition even more challenging by hiding the challenges so you don’t know what your challenges are while in your expedition by clicking the eye button next to the challenges. Hidden challenges give you double the points!

Clicking the dice button will randomize all the challenges in the list even if the challenge is hidden. If you click one of the challenges, it will randomize only that one challenge. So if you like two challenges but not the third challenge you may choose to only change that one challenge.

[h2]Perks and Burdens[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8051219/92803217f1066b8bf0940dcc5ccb879db0224bfa.png[/img]
Perks and burdens are unlocked through points you earned from expeditions! Use the perks to help aid your expedition and apply burdens to increase the amount of points you will earn while making the expedition more difficult.
[list]
[*] Perks come in many forms
[*] Start with item in shelter
[*] Start with neuron glow
[*] Start with karma flower
[*] Make passages useable
[*] Temporarily slow down time
[*] Have different slugcats abilities
[/list]
There are three perks that I will not reveal, so it’s time to theorycraft on what those three perks are!

There are four burdens you can apply to increase the amount of points you’ll receive.
[list]
[*] Blinded shrouds the world in endless nights making dangers harder to see.
[*] Doomed removes the safety net of karma. Any death ends the expedition.
[*] Hunted shows all hostile creatures your location all the time.
[*] Pursued has something stalking you through the world, endlessly searching for you.
[/list]
[h2]Progression[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8051219/7c270f292e68eedadef343a309636fa2cf1fd1f1.jpg[/img]
There are 75 milestones that you can complete to earn rewards. The rewards can be perks, perk slots, burdens, or music tracks from Rain World: Downpour to listen to in the Jukebox. 

Each milestone has different requirements to complete and can be unlocked out of order. For example, you can unlock milestone 2 (complete 1 challenge) before milestone 1 (Reach level 3). These milestones can be challenges you do in one expedition, like complete an expedition as the Spearmaster,  or challenges you do over multiple expeditions, like complete 5 hunting challenges. You may also preview the awards and requirements to complete each milestone by hovering your cursor over each milestone. This can help decide on which rewards you want to go for and how to unlock each milestone to gain those rewards.

Each slugcat has a mission to complete in order to unlock a milestone. Each mission is a set of challenges that a specific slugcat must complete. Choosing a mission will change the slugcat you selected.

[h2]Playing the Expedition[/h2]
The very first thing you’ll notice is that you spawn in a random shelter from any region. If you have any perks that spawn in items, they will be in that shelter with you. Each slugcat will also spawn at karma 2

Normal karma rules apply. If you die, your karma goes down one tier and if you survive the cycle, your karma goes up a tier. Echos will increase your karma cap as usual. However, if the slugcat dies while at karma 1, then the expedition is over. You may play the same challenges if you fail the expedition from the game over screen.

You can keep track of your challenge progress by looking at your map. In the top left corner while you are looking at the map, the lists of the challenges will appear with your progression on each one. Once you complete a challenge, it will be strikethrough from the list. You must survive the cycle, without starving, in order for your progress to be saved. If the slugcat dies, then you lose any challenge progress gained in that cycle.

Once you finish all the challenges, you must survive the cycle to win. 

[h2]Ending of Expedition[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8051219/9bec614b9c333b913e56edf257ef258248df5c8d.png[/img]
Once you complete the expedition, you will gain points based on how difficult the challenges you completed, how many challenges you completed, and any burdens you have active. Creatures killed, cycles, story events, and time taken do not affect the final score.

Once your points are counted, if you complete any milestones you’ll gain your rewards here.

Thank you for reading! 37 days until Downpour is released and I am super excited! I still have more to announce this week so keep an eye out! My good friend Buddy, who is still learning how to be a slugcat, will be streaming Rain World: Downpour on Friday 12pm PST / 3pm EST at https://www.twitch.tv/akuparagames 

- Riv Otter

notes.title: Local Co-op Dev Log 2
notes.content:
Hello, Slugcats!

Welcome to the second devlog of Rain World: Downpour where I’ll talk about the customization options and gameplay details in the new local co-op campaign mode. Longtime players of Rain World might notice that many of these features stem from the Jolly Co-op mod from Garrakx, whom we enlisted to help us craft the Downpour experience for you. If you missed the first dev log, you can view it [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/312520/view/5641338588665839262]here[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8051219/33f4ce84a298c39b98ab8c23e4a06d0920f565cd.png[/img]

The local co-op campaign can be played with up to four players. Choose from any combinations of the eight slugcats, which means you can have more than one of the same slugcat! For example, if you want to explode the whole environment with your friends, for some reason, then multiple slugcats can be Artificer! 

This mode also brings customization options for the slugcats where you can change the slugcat’s size and color. With color mode you can select the colors of the each players’ slugcats. Choose the colors of each of the slugcats with “Custom” or have random colors chosen with “Auto.” You can experience the game as a small young slugpup which has a harder time grabbing higher poles or as an adult slugcat which is bigger and can be grabbed by other creatures easier. 

Camera Input alters how fast the camera changes when a player requests the camera to be focused on them by the map button in game.

There are three difficulty options which are easy, normal, and hard! 
[list]
[*] Easy: Only one player needs to make it to the shelter to progress the next cycle
[*] Normal: You can hibernate if all the slugcat’s bodies make it to the shelter. Even if all but one slugcat is dead, as long as all the fallen allies are in the shelter then the world will progress to the next cycle.
[*] Hard: If any players die then it’s game over. All players need to make it to the shelter alive.
[/list]

The HUD will show an arrow pointing at the slugcat with their name while they are on screen. You can customize the name given to the slugcat and the HUD will show that in game! If a player is off screen, an icon will point at the location of that player. 

You can select if there is friendly fire with thrown spears! Thrown spears by slugcats will fly past your friends if spear miss is selected. Don’t tell anyone but you can still hit your companions with rocks even when spear miss is active.

Now with more players that means more mouths to feed right? Well, technically no. All players will share one food bar so if one slugcat eats all the slugcat gets one food pip filled. We decided to go in this direction as the world is built around the idea of only one slugcat existing in the world. If there were four slugcats each with their own food bar, then they could eat all the food in the region within just a few cycles with no way to survive. Spearmaster is still without a mouth and still has to eat through their spears plus those that like to eat other creatures still have the ability to eat them.

The next dev log we will reveal something new that we’ll launch as part of the free Parity Patch for the base game alongside Downpour!

notes.title: Rain World's difficulty-changing update is now in open beta on Steam
notes.content:
I really liked Rain World, but I'm also really bad at it, and so I ultimately moved on to other things without making very much progress. But now I have a reason to go back—several in fact. The 1.51 update, which was announced in June, is now in open beta on Steam, bringing with it new difficulty levels, multiplayer modes, and "new secrets, strangeness, and hopefully a generally smoother Rain World experience." 

The new difficulties actually come in the form of two new playable characters. The Monk, "weak of body but strong of spirit," will round off some of the game's sharper edges: "In tune with the mysteries of the world and empathetic to its creatures, your journey will be a significantly more peaceful one," developer Videocult said. 

For those who for some reason think that Rain World wasn't hard enough out of the box, there is the Hunter. "Strong and quick, with a fierce metabolism requiring a steady diet of meat. But the stomach won’t be your only concern, as the path of the hunter is one of extreme peril," the studio warned. The update will also introduce a four-player competitive mode, in which players earn points by catching bats and spearing creatures (including each other), and a sandbox mode, also for up to four players, that enables creatures and items to be placed and played with so players can experiment and learn more about how they behave and how to deal with them. 

To access the Rain World 1.51 update, right-click the game listing in your Steam library, hit Properties from the menu, and then select the Betas tab. Enter MANYSLUGCATS into the beta key field (I don't know if it actually needs to be in all-caps but that's what they said, so that's what I did) and then check the code. That will make "beta - new release!" available in the dropdown menu—select that, download the 280MB update, and you're all set.   

Note that you won't be able to switch difficulties in an existing game: If you want to try the Monk or Hunter, you'll need to start a new game. Fortunately, Rain World has three separate save slots, so you can horse around with all three without having to give up on my progress made.

notes.title: Rain World patch fixes some niggling player concerns
notes.content:
Ah, Rain World. Killer of slugcats, destroyer of dreams. The challenging survival platformer has just received its first patch, and it does a pretty good job of fixing some common complaints, without making it "easier" per se. For example, now you're far less likely to get caught in a tunnel you don't want to get caught in, thanks to "disconnected exits" (ie tunnels to nowhere) no longer snagging you.

Elsewhere, slugcat will have a subtle glow when navigating murky water, meaning – generously! – that you'll be able to see yourself. You'll also have a larger lung capacity while swimming. More food has been added to certain regions (read the full notes if you want, names could be considered spoilers), while certain gated areas will be easier to access (ie, the rank you need to be to pass has been lowered).

To be honest, as much as I loved Rain World at launch I think these changes are welcome. They don't sound like they'll take the edge off the game, but it'll mean playing it will be a little less punishing. The full notes are over here, but beware of region name spoilers if that kind of thing annoys you. Oh, and if you've just started, I wrote up some beginners tips last week.

notes.title: Hello friends and slugcats! We present to you patch #1: Rain World v1.01
notes.content:
Hello friends and slugcats! We present to you patch #1: Rain World v1.01
 
This quick patch is intended to accommodate some early player feedback and polish assorted rough edges on the various game systems, etc. These were all low-hanging fruit that we think improves the player experience without taking anything away from the concept of the game. Rain World should be an existential experience: unforgiving and even occasionally unfair. But it should be the jaws of a Lizard that gets you or the Rain, not some ragdoll physics wonk or design oversight!
 
Gameplay improvements:
* “stuck in holes” fix - disconnected exits will no longer snag you
* subtle backlit slugcat in low visibility swimming situations
* quicker turning around in tunnels
* larger lung capacity while swimming
* nerfed the more intense waterfalls in Shoreline to prevent repeated drownings
* more pearls near Scav tolls in Garbage Wastes
* more food in central Garbage Wastes
* more food in central Shaded Citadel
* more karma flowers in world
* karma gate requirements on the Shaded Citadel, Drainage System and Underhang side were lowered to prevent players becoming stuck in challenging regions
* food / karma flowers regeneration now ticks forward on deaths (helps eliminate stuck / starvation situations at low karma)
* players will now keep map progress between deaths (Id say 99.5% of people asked for this)
* map now features gate karma symbols and shelter icons when locations are discovered
* karma depletion on game exit removed if done within 30 seconds of sleep cycle
* full karma drop on exit bug fixed (that was a brutal one, sheesh!)
* intro cinematic is now skippable by holding start / esc
* for players having issues with Grey Screen of Death and starting the game from sav files, you can now entirely skip loading the intro by holding "s" when pressing "New Game." hopefully this helps until we have a real fix!
* many many minor room fixes
 
Stability improvements:
* map loading bug fixed (was causing the corrupted savs, ugh)
* gate crashing bug fixed
* assorted stability improvements
 
etc.
 
Next steps: More patches and content is on the way, of course! We would like to see how this current round of bugfixes land before digging into further issues, as we have a feeling that these might solve a lot of the problems we've seen. But of course if you could keep sending in those bug reports and sav files that would be fantastic and hugely beneficial.
 
Thanks to all for feedback and please keep it coming! Let's all get through this tedious fixing and tweaking so we can get rolling on the fun stuff: new content!
 
<3
--Rain World team
